Q: Why does Apache PDFBox use SHA-1? Is it still secure? A:

Is it used for digital signatures or just internal hashing?

The former.

Is this safe in a production environment?

It depends on what you mean by "safe". Whenever you read or write signed PDFs with SHA-1 digests (i.e. PKCS#1 digital signatures) you are vulnerable1. So you should avoid doing that unwittingly. But there may be situations where you need to take that risk anyway.

We can't do that risk assessment for you. For examples, we don't know what the consequences of document tampering would be to ... your processes.

Should I override it to use SHA-256 instead?

Override how? If you mean by changing (say) getSha1() to return an SHA-256 MessageDigest ... that won't work!

There are other ways to make it impossible for PDFBox to read / write PDF documents with SHA-1 signatures, but these have consequences too.

1 - You may read a document that has been altered after being signed. Or you nay write a document that could be altered after you signed it.
